name: Laser linewidth
seoDesc: Laser linewidth: work out laser frequency (ν) from the cavity linewidth and the power. A free physics calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: Supply the cavity linewidth, the power, the linewidth and the plan and the Laser linewidth calculator solves for laser frequency (ν). Think of it as a shortcut for a lab report, a problem set or a sanity check on a physical situation. The unit chips sit next to the boxes, which is where most hand-calculation mistakes start.

sections.title: How does the Laser linewidth calculator work?
sections.html:
The Laser linewidth calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports laser frequency (ν) in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you type in the cavity linewidth (Γ), the power (P), the linewidth (Δν) and the plan.

Press Calculate once and the page holds the relationship, tracking which boxes you filled and working out everything else; from that point on it follows every edit you make.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Laser linewidth calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Laser frequency (ν)=power (P) × linewidth (Δν) ÷ (PI × (cavity linewidth (Γ) ^ 2) × plan)
Speol=fundamental wavelength × laser frequency (ν)
C1=A1 ÷ (B1 × plan)
Freq max=frequency bandwidth + freq min
Freq max=2 × speol ÷ (2 × fundamental wavelength − wavelength bandwidth)
Wavelength bandwidth=-2 × fundamental wavelength + 2 × speol ÷ freq min

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

  • Frequency, opening in terahertz
  • Frequency, opening in gigahertz
  • Power, opening in watts
  • Frequency, opening in hertz
  • Length, opening in nanometers
  • Length, opening in nanometers
  • Frequency, opening in terahertz
  • Energy, opening in joules

Results are rounded for display but computed at full precision, so chaining one result into the next does not accumulate error. Very large and very small numbers switch to scientific notation rather than printing a run of zeros.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Laser linewidth calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Writing up a lab result and needing a quick cross-check
  • Testing whether an answer is physically plausible before you trust it
  • Solving a problem set where the algebra is more interesting than the arithmetic
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — the cavity linewidth, the power and the linewidth — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Laser linewidth calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns laser frequency (ν), derived from the cavity linewidth, the power and the linewidth. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Laser linewidth calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the cavity linewidth, the power, the linewidth and the plan, which is 8 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter laser frequency (ν) in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Laser frequency (ν) opens in terahertz and the chip beside it offers 21 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: Is the Laser linewidth calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.
